    Kupisch cyclicity for distributive Hom spaces #

    If endpoint-stable subspaces of one Hom space are linearly ordered, compare the source-radical and target-radical parts of the principal bimodule. Split residue maps and nilpotence of the endpoint Jacobson radicals then show that the principal bimodule is cyclic on one side. Equivalently, the morphism allows transit or cotransit in the sense used by BGRS.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.transit_or_cotransit_of_homSubbimodule_comparable {k : Type w} [Field k] {C : Type u} [CategoryTheory.Category.{v, u} C] [CategoryTheory.Preadditive C] [CategoryTheory.Linear k C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsArtinianRing (CategoryTheory.End X)] [IsArtinianRing (CategoryTheory.End Y)] (sourceResidue : CategoryTheory.End X →ₐ[k] k) (targetResidue : CategoryTheory.End Y →ₐ[k] k) (sourceResidue_zero : ∀ (a : CategoryTheory.End X), sourceResidue a = 0 ↔ a ∈ Ring.jacobson (CategoryTheory.End X)) (targetResidue_zero : ∀ (b : CategoryTheory.End Y), targetResidue b = 0 ↔ b ∈ Ring.jacobson (CategoryTheory.End Y)) (hcomparable : ∀ (S T : Submodule k (X ⟶ Y)), IsHomSubbimodule S → IsHomSubbimodule T → S ≤ T ∨ T ≤ S) :
    AllowsTransit f ∨ AllowsCotransit f

    Kupisch's cyclicity argument: linearly ordered endpoint-stable subspaces, split residue maps, and nilpotent endpoint radicals force every morphism to allow transit or cotransit.

    Once endpoint-stable Hom subspaces are known to be linearly ordered, the split-basic residue maps supply the entire BGRS distributive-Hom package.
